RiccardoSottini · Nov 28, 2026

Yes! That's the reason why I chose it - due to iterations with repl and extremely efficient context window usage / token expenditure. Effectively, for the use case scenario of my project, Clojure can express logic and functionalities that are shown on screen with just a couple of lines of code, removing all the boilerplate/overhead code.

skeledrew · Nov 28, 2026

It's still pretty fresh, so though I've used it to do some work on another project I don't really consider it satisfactorily proven yet. I'll probably open source it when I feel it's more solid. Only Python is supported, though theoretically the CLI side (it's split into CLI, server and debugger portions) could send commands to a debugger made in any language that supports the API. The only languages that can be fully supported though are those that allow full runtime evaluation, typically anything interpreted. Compile-only languages are out.
